"Score the card 1-5 on each criterion. For each score give ref, the card line (card:<field>) that decides it, or plan:<field path> when no card line carries it, and a reason of at most 25 words. Use NA only where a criterion allows it. Then name decides_by: the id of the earliest phase after which decision_rule can be applied whichever outcome occurs, or \"none\". A phase that only reproduces a published number, or only measures throughput the question does not ask about, does not count. Give decides_by_reason in at most 25 words. Decide only from the text below; do not use tools.
Root question: generative pipeline for discovery of single phase immersion coolants
Option record: {\"id\":\"IC-V3\",\"title\":\"MD verification inserted into Org-Mol's ester shortlist before synthesis\",\"summary\":\"Data-centre immersion cooling needs dielectric liquids with low viscosity, high thermal conductivity and heat capacity, and PFAS rules are pushing the field towards PFAS-free esters. Restrict the generative search to synthetically accessible PFAS-free esters of the kind already ML-screened at scale, filter to a ranked shortlist, and MD-verify the top 100, 300 then 1000 candidates' viscosity and thermal conductivity before any synthesis decision. Score against measured data for known esters and commercial single-phase fluids held out of training, never against the predictors. More compute buys more MD-verified candidates and longer simulations per candidate, testing whether the best cooling figure of merit keeps climbing beyond the 461-candidate shortlist stage.\",\"root_link\":\"SAME: ester discovery kept on transport properties and on the down-selection step where prior work stops.\",\"compute_open\":\"MD-verified candidates (100–1000, anchored to a ~461-candidate shortlist) and simulation length per candidate. Unknown: whether MD meaningfully reorders an ML shortlist or merely confirms it.\",\"sequential\":\"not given\",\"source_urls\":[]}
Card:
card:question: Does molecular-dynamics verification of viscosity and thermal conductivity reorder a machine-learning ester shortlist, and does the best coolant keep improving?
card:hypothesis: Molecular dynamics reorders the shortlist: machine-learning viscosity error (22.467% MAPE) exceeds molecular-dynamics error, so better esters appear after verification [s3].
card:sequential_part: Each candidate's viscosity waits on one long trajectory; the ranking waits on 100, 300, then 1000 candidates.
card:method: Split each long trajectory into independent replicas on separate GPUs, block-average the Green-Kubo integrals, and run candidates side by side.
card:if_lever: By 100 candidates the replica ranking matches the sequential baseline, diverges from machine-learning, and the best figure climbs through 1000.
card:if_not: Replicas match the sequential ranking only by 300 candidates; then molecular dynamics confirms the machine-learning list from 100 through 1000.
card:test_summary: Run Green-Kubo molecular dynamics on the top 100 then 300 of 461 monoesters [s1]. Compare MD-vs-ML rank correlation and figure climb. Time single-trajectory against parallel replicas.
card:closest_prior: A 2026 benchmark ran Green-Kubo molecular dynamics on eight organic liquids; viscosity ranking stayed, thermal conductivity did not [s9][s7][s8].
card:left_open: Only eight molecules had viscosity and thermal conductivity Green-Kubo verified against reference values [s9]; the 100-to-1000 shortlist answer is open.
card:anchor: Green-Kubo molecular dynamics reproduces the paper's measured Ester 1 viscosity 6.41 cSt and conductivity 0.141 W/m K.
card:limits: Shows single-phase ranking under one force field and 15 ns sampling; no synthesis, dielectric, flammability, compatibility, or stability checks. The 1000-candidate run exceeds the budget.

Criteria:
stakes: Take the two outcomes this test predicts, as measured here and within the limits in scope_gap. 5 = whichever occurs, a choice someone faces (what to buy, build, collect or scale next) changes, and the test measures the quantity that choice depends on; 3 = the outcomes bear on that choice only through a step this test does not check (a stand-in system, simulation to reality, a single model), or one outcome is already much more likely than the other; 1 = neither outcome would change anything. Do not score how famous the field is or how close it is to the root question.
lever: Could the result tell if_lever from if_not, with compute the only thing that changed? Check four conditions: (a) the predicted difference between if_lever and if_not is larger than what noise_rule says run-to-run noise can produce; (b) compute_axis spans at least 10×; (c) the varied quantity is bought with compute, not with more data, labels or people (when restructuring.method is not none: the arms run on the same hardware and differ only in method); (d) inputs that could also explain the difference are in held_fixed. 5 = all four hold; 3 = one fails or cannot be told from the plan; 1 = two or more fail, or the measured quantity is not the one the question asks about.
verifiable: What is the measured outcome scored against? 5 = an exact or planted truth that does not come from the method under test (a simulation's hidden true run, an exact success flag, a formal checker, planted items), and the setup first reproduces a published number within a stated tolerance; 3 = labels from a model or human rater with an agreement check, or exact truth with no reproduction step; 1 = nothing independent of the method's own output.
open: Does the closest published result already answer this question over this range? 5 = the quoted prior stops short of this range or asks a different question, and the plan states the gap; 3 = the prior answers part of it (a narrower range, a related system), or no prior is named; 1 = the quoted prior already answers it. Reusing published tools, models or benchmarks does not lower this score.
reshape: Does the plan remove a step-after-step dependency that one answer waits on, rather than run independent work side by side? 5 = restructuring names the dependency, why it need not run in order and how the plan computes it at the same time; condition says what must hold for that to pay off; condition_phase measures it before the main spend; and the closest prior does not already do this for this system; 3 = it removes a dependency, but condition is missing or is not measured before the main spend; 2 = it parallelises only within each step (splitting a large state across GPUs) or regroups and rebalances independent work (batching unfinished runs, load balancing, lower precision), leaving the chain in order; 1 = independent copies side by side, or one job per GPU, is the only parallelism, or the plan rebuilds a parallel version the closest prior already reports for this system. Reusing a method published for a different system does not lower this score.
baseline: Is the gain timed against the strongest ways to get the same answer without the plan's method? Check four conditions: (a) baseline_sequential is tuned (compiled, vectorised or multithreaded code, or a published optimised code), not a plain interpreted loop; (b) baseline_copies is timed on the same GPUs; (c) anchor checks the parallel result against the sequential one within a stated tolerance; (d) a named phase times every arm as time or dollars to one answer, so the gain is measured, not only modelled. 5 = all four hold; 3 = one fails or cannot be told from the plan; 1 = two or more fail. NA when restructuring.method is none.

Let me score each criterion.

Stakes: Two outcomes: MD reorders ML shortlist vs MD confirms. If reorders, decision about which candidates to synthesize changes; if confirms, ML list is trusted. But limits: no synthesis, dielectric, etc. — test measures simulation quantities only, not reality. Also one outcome (confirm) maybe more likely? The choice: which candidates to advance to synthesis / spend compute on MD. The test measures viscosity and conductivity — the quantity the choice depends on — but only within simulation, single force field. Score3 seems right: outcomes bear on the choice through simulation-to-reality step not checked (scope_gap). Actually criterion says 3 = bears on choice only through a step this test does not check (stand-in system, simulation to reality, single model). Here MD is a stand-in for real viscosity. Score 3.

Lever: (a) predicted difference: Spearman <0.7 vs confirm; noise_rule says ranking stability Spearman >=0.95 between runs, so difference 0.7 vs presumably high — larger than noise. Fom ratio 1.05 vs noise? noise rule gives standard errors; 5% threshold — maybe borderline. (b) compute axis100 to 1000 = 10×, levels100,300,1000 — spans exactly 10×. (c) varied quantity bought with compute — yes, MD-verified candidates count. Restructuring.method is not none (replicas vs sequential) — hmm, "when restructuring.method is not none: the arms run on same hardware and differ only in method". The arms: ml_rank, seq_traj, rep_avg — differ in method, same hardware (8-GPU node). But the lever is about compute axis (candidates count), not method. The condition (c) applies though: arms run on same hardware? seq_traj on one A100, rep_avg on separate GPUs of same node — same hardware. (d) held_fixed includes force field, protocol, pool, node. Seems all four hold. Score 5? Let's check (a) more: if_lever predicts Spearman MD-ML <0.7 AND fom ratio >= 1.05. Noise: run-to-run stability Spearman >= 0.95. So the difference between <0.7 and presumably >0.7... if_not says "confirms the ML list" implying correlation high. Gap between 0.7 and 0.95 > noise. Fom ratio 1.05 vs standard error — block-averaged SE, plausible. (b) exactly 10× (100→1000) — "at least 10×" holds. I'd say 5. But possibly (a) partly unclear for fom threshold. Given5 requires all four hold; fom 5% threshold vs SE not stated numerically. Could be 4 but schema allows 1-5 only. Hmm. Reasonably5 or 4... I'll give 4? The criterion says 3 = one fails or cannot be told. Is noise for fom tellable? noise_rule says each candidate's figure carries block-averaged SE — so noise is characterized; the 5% threshold versus SE not explicitly compared.
